target_customer: Companies with an API or developer product that need public developer documentation and portals
problem: Writing and maintaining good API documentation is painful, and bad docs slow developer adoption of an API.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription tiers (early plan about $14 per month for 3 doc versions and 1 admin on a readme.io subdomain)
product_category: Developer documentation and API reference hubs

founders.name: Gregory Koberger
founders.background_notes: YC page and TechCrunch name him as the sole founder. Prior employers and education not found in opened sources. He describes himself as a developer who hated writing documentation (post title on ReadMe blog, not opened).

competitors.name: Swagger UI
competitors.what: Open source tool for rendering interactive API docs from a spec
competitors.traction_then: Named by InfoQ as an open source alternative; no figures

competitors.name: Slate
competitors.what: Open source static API documentation generator
competitors.traction_then: Named by InfoQ as an open source alternative; no figures

technical_complexity.rationale: A hosted docs editor with versioning and spec import is standard web engineering; the hard parts were collaborative editing and interactive API explorers.

defensibility.rationale: Open source generators existed and docs content is portable, but hosted teams accumulate content, custom domains and API logs over time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying or buying it; ReadMe stayed independent and active as of the YC listing.

market_need_then: Companies were launching APIs and the YC launch post cites Stripe docs as the standard and says API providers face more competition for mindshare, so docs quality was a visible adoption lever.

branding.name_origin: Named after the README file that ships with software packages, per Koberger on a JAMstack Radio episode (search snippet, episode page not opened).
branding.domain_note: Started on readme.io and now uses readme.com; acquisition date and price not found.

identity.logo: Owl mark per company about page snippet
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual and developer friendly, careers page described as a playful take on working there

branding.community_and_virality: Docs hosted on readme.io subdomains expose the brand to developers; no merch or fan accounts found.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable, meaningful name for developers and an owl mascot, but a generic word and little independent press on the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: ReadMe grew from a documentation tool into a developer hub platform, reported about 3,000 paying customers and several profitable years by its 2019 Series A led by Accel, and remains active with about 52 staff. Hosted docs on customer subdomains spread the product, and low capital needs let it raise only a small seed before the Series A. No shutdown or acquisition was found.
notes: Series A of $9M in 2019 is confirmed by TechCrunch and ReadMe blog snippet (search results). Seed of $1.2M in 2014 from TechCrunch; an aggregator lists about $1.175M in May 2015. One aggregator claims about $49M raised, unverified and not recorded. Founders: the Medium founder story returned 403 and was not worked around. No Series B found in searches.
